_doc: Corpus-completeness manifest (Arc 1 S4). One row per conformance-corpus
family: every test_fixtures/ subdirectory plus every workspace/tests/
entry. scripts/check_corpus_manifest.py enforces it in CI (the
workspace-json-fresh lane): required consumers present, active-port
symmetry where declared, no unknown families, no orphaned fixtures.
kind: source = hand-authored inputs; compiled = generated from a source
corpus or a canonical generator; fixtures = driver cases + pinned
goldens. required_consumers is the BLOCKING set (POLICY.md #1: active
ports rust+swift, the reference interpreter, and the scripts/ gates;
the frozen OCaml/Python-Qt ports run at the five-port-parity tag and
are deliberately untracked here). port_symmetry: the rust and swift
claimed sets (after the transitive data-reference closure) must be
identical for the family. claim_style is documentation of HOW each
consumer registers fixtures — the checker's extraction rules implement
TWO gap lists, of opposite shapes: known_gaps SUPPRESSES a named
mechanical check (and a row that suppresses nothing is reported stale);
coverage_gaps DECLARES what the corpus cannot reach at all and is
printed on every run. See _coverage_gaps_doc at the foot of this file.

test_fixtures/actions.notes: The ACTION-seam corpus (dispatch_action / dispatchYamlAction). Goldens (*_expected.json) and setup SVGs are claimed transitively via expected_json/setup_svg data references. Second branches of the toggle_all_layers_* actions (all-invisible->preview, all-outline->preview, all-locked->unlock) were reference-only pins (workspace/tests/phase3/) until S4 added the *_all_* port-side fixtures; the remaining phase3 panel-state-driven scenarios stay reference-only pending a port-side panel-seeding mechanism (a named future decision).

claim_style.rust: path literals (cross_language_test.rs + module-scattered tests, e.g. geometry/tspan.rs)
claim_style.swift: path literals (AlignFixtureTests full paths; TspanPrimitivesTests loadFixture)

test_fixtures/algorithms.notes: Port symmetry is deliberately NOT machine-checked per registration list here: every algorithm in cross_language_algorithms.py's ALGORITHMS dict is gated across both active ports by that script (each port's roundtrip binary runs every fixture), while the in-port unit registrations legitimately differ (Rust natively gates the pane/panel/menu vectors; Swift natively gates align + the tspan primitives). The count is not restated here on purpose -- it was stale at '14' while the dict held 15. The three PANEL vectors are in-port only (not in the ALGORITHMS dict, so not driven by the roundtrip binaries): panel_layout.json pins rects, panel_widget_tree.json pins structure, and panel_bind_values.json pins RESOLVED bind.* VALUES -- the last is also driven by the reference (test_bind_values.py), which additionally asserts the golden is not stale relative to it.

test_fixtures/artboards.notes: Reference-only BY DESIGN: the default-seeded artboard scenario drives interpreter panel/effect state that the ports cannot seed headlessly today; port-side panel-seeding is a named future decision. The ports gate artboard DOCUMENT semantics via the operations corpus (artboard_*.json) instead.

test_fixtures/character_apply.notes: CHARPANEL: the FIELD-SCOPED Character-panel apply law (transcripts/CHARACTER.md 'The field-scoped apply law'). Gates all THREE live implementations off one corpus: a panel edit names its field and only that field's attribute group is written, everything else preserved per element. Same defect class as the stroke_apply family, over sixteen attributes, plus a port divergence (Swift mitigated it in the panel VIEW, Rust not at all). The reference states the field -> group table (workspace_interpreter/character_law.py) and the ports mirror it. The reference arm additionally asserts the corpus REJECTS the whole-rebuild law it replaced, so the gate cannot pass vacuously. No scripts consumer: the law is a pure function pinned in-port, not an algorithm_roundtrip binary.

test_fixtures/concept_constraints.notes: conformance.json compiled from workspace/tests/concept_constraints.yaml; the check_*.sh freshness gate recompiles and byte-compares.

claim_style.rust: name-lists (json/binary/svg round-trip arrays) + assert_svg_parse helper calls + path literals
claim_style.swift: name-lists (jsonRoundtripAllExpected / binaryRoundtripAllExpected / binaryReadPythonFixtures) + assertSvgParse/assertWorkspaceFixture helper calls + path literals
claim_style.scripts: commutativity FIXTURE_NAMES + _golden() calls + structural-golden checkers (check_menu_structure.py, check_toolbar_structure.py)

test_fixtures/expected.notes: Rust-authored canonical goldens (parse/roundtrip expectations, .bin byte pins, dependency-index and workspace-layout goldens, structural goldens). Port symmetry is hand-maintained per name-list (the S5-symmetrized json/binary/svg arrays) rather than machine-checked: a per-file symmetry rule would false-red the legitimately single-consumer members (menu_structure.json and toolbar_structure.json are scripts-only structural goldens; dup_id_import.json is parse-only). Orphan detection here is REAL (no glob claims this directory).

test_fixtures/expressions.notes: conformance.json compiled from workspace/tests/expressions.yaml. The reference gates the SOURCE yaml directly (test_expr.py), not this compiled artifact — so 'reference' is intentionally not required here but IS required on the workspace/tests/expressions.yaml row.

test_fixtures/gestures.notes: The canvas-tool-seam corpus (press/move/release through YamlTool). Goldens and setup SVGs claimed transitively.

test_fixtures/keys.notes: The key->action resolution corpus; goldens claimed transitively via expected_json.

claim_style.rust: path literals (run_operation_fixture calls + txn/drag_coalesce/recorded literals) + data references
claim_style.swift: runOperationFixture helper calls + path literals + data references

test_fixtures/operations.notes: The op_apply corpus — the journal/undo spine's byte gate. 60+ of these files exist ONLY as data references (expected_json / expected_journal_json inside the driver fixtures); the transitive pass claims them. Port symmetry here is the gate's founding case: the Swift registration set lacked tspan_ops.json until S4 forced the remediation.

claim_style.rust: path literal (read_fixture in src/cross_language_test.rs preservation_invariants) + data references
claim_style.swift: path literal (readFixture in CrossLanguageTests.swift preservationInvariants) + data references

test_fixtures/preservation.notes: The PRESERVATION corpus (transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md §4.1, the DOCUMENT-LEVEL INVARIANT GATE). Unlike every other fixtures family here it pins no golden document: it asserts six invariants (id_uniqueness / id_survival / consumed_ids_die / fresh_ids / bystanders_unchanged / subject_fields_only) over the canonical test JSON before and after an edit. That is what lets ONE vector be evaluated identically by both ports while each fails on its OWN sites — a golden could not, since the ports diverge on exactly the keys the law legislates. Setup SVGs are claimed transitively via setup_svg. A vector may PIN a known violation per port (expected_violations); a pinned invariant is asserted to FAIL, so fixing the site turns the gate red until the pin is removed — a pin cannot rot into a silent suppression. scripts/check_preservation_corpus.py gates the DATA shape with five anti-vacuity guards (V1-V5).

test_fixtures/production_capture.notes: The production run_effects capture pins (OP_LOG.md section 9, 3b-B). Journal/document/re-derivation goldens are claimed transitively via the root-relative expected_*_json fields.

test_fixtures/stroke_apply.notes: STROKEWIDTH: the FIELD-SCOPED Stroke-panel apply law (transcripts/STROKE.md 'The field-scoped apply law'). Gates all THREE live implementations off one corpus: a panel edit names its field and only that field's attribute group is written, everything else preserved per element; plus the colour-only recolour route. The reference states the field -> group table (workspace_interpreter/stroke_law.py) and the ports mirror it. The reference arm additionally asserts the corpus REJECTS the whole-rebuild law it replaced, so the gate cannot pass vacuously. No scripts consumer: the law is a pure function pinned in-port, not an algorithm_roundtrip binary.

claim_style.rust: DIRECTORY GLOB (tests/cross_language_test.rs json_roundtrip_all_fixtures reads every svg/*.svg) + name-lists + data references

test_fixtures/svg.notes: Hand-authored SVG inputs. Rust's roundtrip test GLOBS the whole directory, so this family's orphan detection is VACUOUS by construction: any stray .svg is auto-exercised by the glob and can never be flagged orphaned here. Deletions must rely on the sibling expected/ family's REAL orphan signal (that is exactly how named_elements.svg was caught: its expected/named_elements.json partner was orphaned) plus review. Port symmetry not machine-checked: Swift's parse/roundtrip name lists are hand-symmetrized with Rust's (S5), while setup SVGs are shared via data references.

test_fixtures/workspace_operations.notes: The layout-op corpus (panel/pane vocabulary). Per-case goldens claimed transitively via expected_json; layout setups live in expected/ (the setup field) and are claimed transitively there.

workspace/tests/concept_constraints.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; its compiled conformance.json is the artifact the ports and the reference gate.

workspace/tests/concept_fitters.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; compiled artifact gated downstream.

workspace/tests/concept_operations.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; compiled artifact gated downstream.

workspace/tests/concepts.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; compiled artifact gated downstream.

claim_style.reference: os.path.join segments (test_expr.py runs the yaml directly)

workspace/tests/expressions.yaml.notes: The expression-language corpus source. The reference interpreter is the executable spec and runs the yaml directly; the ports run the compiled test_fixtures/expressions/conformance.json.

workspace/tests/gradient_primitives.yaml.notes: The gradient_tile / gradient_slider widget-primitive exercise fixture. Until S4 its only consumer was the NON-GATING flask reference renderer (jas_flask/tests/test_renderer.py) — i.e. no blocking consumer at all; test_gradient_primitives.py now structurally validates every gradient/stop and evaluates what the reference evaluator covers. Widget RENDERING of gradient_tile/gradient_slider remains unvalidated by any blocking consumer (the reference interpreter has no renderer) — an honest, known limit.

workspace/tests/phase3.notes: Reference-only layer-action scenarios. The glob is a DIRECTORY-level claim: orphan detection inside it is VACUOUS (any stray yaml is silently exercised, none can be flagged), and the consumer itself silently passes when the directory is missing — the corpus gate independently asserts the directory exists and is non-empty. Coverage honesty: the toggle_all_layers_* second branches pinned here were reference-only until S4 added port-side actions fixtures (toggle_all_layers_*_all_*.json); the panel-state-driven scenarios (delete_layer_selection_two_layers, duplicate_layer_selection_one_layer, new_layer_with_selection) REMAIN reference-only pending a port-side panel-seeding mechanism — a named future decision.

workspace/tests/set_effect.notes: Reference-only BY DESIGN: the set-effect matrix pins the interpreter's `set:` semantics (typing, nullability, shadowing, panel routing) at the spec level; the ports exercise set: through the panel/action corpora rather than this matrix. Glob claim — orphan detection vacuous, directory-existence asserted by the gate.

_coverage_gaps_doc: The SECOND gap list, and the opposite shape from known_gaps above.
known_gaps is a suppressor: each row names one mechanical check on one
family/file and downgrades its failure to a warning, so it can only
ever speak about a check this gate already runs. coverage_gaps records
what the gate does NOT check -- a family whose fixtures never reach the
interesting branch, a field no fixture sets, a divergence no
port-vs-port comparison can see. It suppresses nothing; every row is
printed on every run, precisely so a green gate stops implying a
completeness it never had.
Required keys: id, title, evidence, blocks, unblock (census optional).
`evidence` must be a claim someone can re-run, because a gap you cannot
state precisely is not ready to record. Every row below was re-measured
on this commit rather than copied from the census -- three census
figures did not survive that (noted in the rows), and the census's
hit_test/marquee row is not here at all because it has since CLOSED:
element_intersects_rect and element_intersects_polygon are now driven
by both roundtrip binaries over 6 of hit_test.json's 40 vectors.
Census rows 5.3, 5.6, 5.10 and 5.11 are deliberately absent: they are
real, but this pass did not re-verify them, and an unverified row here
would be the same false assurance the empty list was.

coverage_gaps.title: The preservation gate can only reach violations expressible in op_apply's verb vocabulary, so six of EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md §3.5's rows stay invisible to it
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit by grepping the dispatchers. op_apply has exactly ONE boolean verb in each port (jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs `"boolean_union"`, JasSwift/Sources/Document/OpApply.swift `case "boolean_union"`) and ZERO verbs matching apply_mask / set_width_points / make_compound_shape / boolean_subtract / boolean_intersect / boolean_divide. No verb can produce a PARTIAL (control-point) selection either: the string `Partial` occurs once in the whole of op_apply.rs, inside a `#[derive(...)]`. Consequently these §3.5 rows are unreachable from this corpus: Swift `withMask` .path arm; Swift `withWidthPoints` .path arm; Rust `move_control_points` Rect->Polygon arm (needs a corner drag, i.e. a partial selection); Rust `make_compound_shape_with_op` duplicate id; the boolean SURVIVOR arms (subtract_front / subtract_back / crop / trim / divide) and their Swift `locked: false` + dropped name/id/toolOrigin/mask; and both blob-brush `fillRule` arms (a gesture, not an op).
coverage_gaps.blocks: Of the §3.5 table, this gate today catches the Rust UNION frontmost-id carry, the Swift withChildren class (5 vectors), and one of the 41 Swift inline Layer(/Group( literals. The rest of the table is not gated by anything cross-language.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Two independent routes, both fixture-plus-verb: (a) widen the op vocabulary with the missing boolean verbs and a mask/width-points setter, then add preservation vectors for the 1->1 survivor arms — where subject_fields_only is exactly the right predicate; (b) give the GESTURE corpus the same invariant gate, which reaches the blob-brush arms and the Rect corner drag that the op corpus cannot address.

coverage_gaps.title: The six preservation invariants say nothing about the FIELDS of a freshly minted element, so the boolean result's lossy kind demotion and its dropped non-paint fields are invisible
coverage_gaps.evidence: The invariants are id_uniqueness / id_survival / consumed_ids_die / fresh_ids / bystanders_unchanged / subject_fields_only. Every one of them is keyed on an id that existed BEFORE the edit; a minted element has no before-image to diff against, so nothing in the set constrains it. Concretely, on the boolean_union_merges_two_rects vector both ports emit a single-ring `Polygon` — the §3.5 row 'Boolean flatten, single-ring arm, both ports' calls that a lossy demotion (a Polygon has no slot for widthPoints / strokeBrush / strokeBrushOverrides / fillRule) — and the gate reports nothing, because the invariants never look at the output's kind or its non-identity fields.
coverage_gaps.blocks: §3.3's unanimity carry, §3.6's per-op paint column, and T1's representation term (no lossy demotion) are all statements ABOUT the minted element. None of them is gated here.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Add a seventh declarative invariant to the vector shape — an `expected_output` block naming the required kind and the fields the result must carry (unanimous values, RESULT_FILL_RULE) — and implement it in both port gates. This is additive to the existing five vectors and needs no new op verbs.

coverage_gaps.title: Swift indexes text by grapheme cluster; Rust and the reference index by Unicode scalar, so no non-ASCII vector can be added to the three text families
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured through the roundtrip harnesses at char_width 10 on this commit. content "ae\u0301b" (4 scalars / 3 clusters): reference and Rust give char_count 4 with 4 glyphs, Swift gives 3 with 3. The ZWJ family emoji U+1F468 U+200D U+1F469 U+200D U+1F467 (5 scalars / 1 cluster): reference and Rust give 5, Swift gives 1. Total line advance now AGREES (40 and 50 both ports) because the injected measurer counts scalars; it is the per-glyph subdivision and every index derived from it that diverge. Root cause is `Array(content)` in TextLayout.swift and PathTextLayout.swift. (TextLayoutParagraph.swift was cited here in error: it contains ZERO `Array(` occurrences - it holds only the hyphenation/segment/counter helpers.)
coverage_gaps.blocks: text_layout, text_layout_paragraph and path_text_layout are ASCII-only families. The rust-vs-swift comparison has no oracle-holdout mechanism (only property_planar and exact_boolean get one), so a non-ASCII vector cannot be added and marked -- it would simply red the gate.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Move Swift's three layout files onto scalar indices, in the SAME sweep as TextEditSession/TypeTool/TypeOnPathTool, which do their cursor arithmetic in `Character` counts (`text.count`, `key.count == 1`) and would otherwise desync from the layout for exactly these strings.
coverage_gaps.census: 5.9(a), extended: the census called this a harness bug only. The harness half is fixed (HARNESSUNIT); this is the product half it was hiding.

coverage_gaps.title: element_bounds gates a function that ignores transform entirely; the transform-aware bbox is now gated by its own family, but only for a single-layer path
coverage_gaps.evidence: All 17 vectors in test_fixtures/algorithms/element_bounds.json carry "transform": null. That is not a fixture oversight: Element::bounds / Element.bounds IGNORE common.transform in both ports -- measured through the two roundtrip binaries on this commit, a 10x10 rect at the origin carrying translate(100,50) reports [0,0,10,10] from Rust and from Swift alike. So transform-bearing vectors added HERE would pin the transform being ignored, not the transform-aware path. The transform-aware function is element_evaluated_bbox / elementEvaluatedBBox, and it is now driven by the element_evaluated_bounds family (9 vectors: translate, non-uniform scale, rotate 45, skewX, a full composed matrix, an ancestor-only layer transform, an element-then-layer composition-order vector, a stroked geometric-vs-preview vector, and a no-transform control).
coverage_gaps.blocks: Two narrower things than before. (1) The new family places every vector as layers[0].children[0], so the ancestor walk is exercised at ONE level -- a nested group chain, and a group whose CHILDREN carry transforms (geometric_children_bounds does not fold those), are still ungated. (2) Whether Element::bounds SHOULD stay transform-blind is an open product question, not a corpus one: both ports agree today, so there is no divergence to catch, and the corpus pins the agreement.
coverage_gaps.unblock: For (1), extend element_evaluated_bounds with group-nesting vectors once the runners can express a nested document. For (2), a ruling on whether the untransformed bbox is the intended contract of Element::bounds.

coverage_gaps.title: The flatten family gates flatten_path_commands; the flattener the boolean pipeline calls is in neither roundtrip binary
coverage_gaps.evidence: Both harnesses call flatten_path_commands / flattenPathCommands (jas_dioxus/src/bin/algorithm_roundtrip.rs and JasSwift/ToolsAlgorithm/AlgorithmRoundtrip.swift). flatten_path_to_rings / flattenPathToRings have 6 references each across the two ports' sources and zero in either harness.
coverage_gaps.blocks: A family-name audit reports flatten as covered while the subdivision the boolean pipeline depends on is uncovered.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Either drive flatten_path_to_rings from a family of its own, or state in the manifest row that flatten covers the command-level flattener only.

coverage_gaps.title: flatten.json has no arc command, so the A-degrades-to-a-line branch of the flattener is ungated
coverage_gaps.evidence: Re-counted mechanically over the parsed fixture on this commit: 18 vectors, with 8 of them carrying a C and 4 a Q (8 C commands and 4 Q commands in total), and ZERO A commands. The census row this replaces said 3 vectors and no curve command at all -- true when it was written, and closed since by the cubic/quadratic vectors; the arc leg is what survives of it.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Both flatteners send SmoothCurveTo / SmoothQuadTo / ArcTo to their endpoint as a straight line, in a catch-all arm no vector enters. The same arm also carries the current-point write for those commands, which is the defect class cubic_then_quad_current_point_chain was added to catch for cubics.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Fixture-only: add an arc vector, and one where an arc is followed by a command that reads the current point.

coverage_gaps.title: No fit_curve vector reaches the iterative refinement or the recursive split, so Schneider's algorithm is gated only through its first pass
coverage_gaps.evidence: Instrumented fit_cubic with per-branch probes and ran the fixture through the Rust harness on this commit: generate_bezier reached 3 times (the 3 vectors with n_pts > 2 -- collinear_points_one_segment, horizontal_line, vertical_line), and reparameterize, newton_raphson and the recursive split reached ZERO times, because every one of those fits within tolerance on the first pass. The other 4 of 7 vectors return at the points.len() < 2 guard or the n_pts == 2 early exit. NOTE: the census claimed none of the 7 reaches generate_bezier; that is over-wide -- 3 do.
coverage_gaps.blocks: reparameterize, newton_raphson and the recursive split carry the algorithm's actual difficulty and are unexercised by the corpus.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Fixture-only: add a vector whose curvature exceeds the error tolerance on one segment, so the split fires.

coverage_gaps.title: The codec gates cover only the field subset some fixture happens to populate, and the most divergence-prone fields are populated by none
coverage_gaps.evidence: Across all 39 test_fixtures/expected/*.json (the census said 25 -- re-counted on this commit), the keys mode, mask, fill_gradient, stroke_gradient, fill_rule, tool_origin, dash_align_anchors and width_points appear in ZERO files.
coverage_gaps.blocks: A canonical-JSON before/after comparison catches a dropped field perfectly, but only for fields a fixture sets. The gate passes loudly and says nothing about the region where the known CommonProps/Document field losses live.
coverage_gaps.unblock: One maximal fixture per element type with every optional field set to a non-default value -- the single highest-leverage addition in the serialization domain.

coverage_gaps.title: The canonical test-JSON writers escape only backslash and quote, so no fixture can express text containing a control character
coverage_gaps.evidence: JsonObj::str_val in jas_dioxus/src/geometry/test_json.rs and JsonObj.str in JasSwift/Sources/Geometry/TestJson.swift each apply exactly two replacements (\\ and \") and no U+0000-U+001F escaping. Consistent with that, zero of the 39 test_fixtures/expected/*.json contain an escaped control character.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The byte oracle behind all three codec gates structurally cannot express multi-line text, so no fixture can be added for it until the writers are fixed. It fails LOUDLY (both parsers reject), so it is a ceiling rather than a silent divergence.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Add U+0000-U+001F escaping to both writers, then add a text fixture containing a newline.

coverage_gaps.title: NARROWED (VIEWSEED, 2026-07-27): the runners can now express a non-identity view, and 9 vectors do, but 63 of the 72 action/gesture driver cases still run at the identity view
coverage_gaps.evidence: Re-measured on this commit. The grep this row used to cite -- zoom_level / view_offset across test_fixtures/ and workspace/tests/ -- now returns two files, test_fixtures/actions/view_state.json and test_fixtures/gestures/draw_rect_zoomed.json, where it returned none. Counting driver cases (a JSON array of objects carrying a `name`) across test_fixtures/actions/ and test_fixtures/gestures/: 72 total, 9 carrying a `view` block -- the 7 view-state action vectors, the zoomed Rect gesture, and none elsewhere. Both runners in both ports accept the seed (`seed_case_view` / `seedCaseView`), so a case that wants a non-identity view now only has to ask.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The zoom division is now gated for exactly ONE tool (Rect, through pointer_event_payload, which is shared by every YAML tool) and for the doc.zoom.* effect family. Everything downstream of a tool handler that re-reads the view for itself -- overlay hit radii, the handle/curve hit tests, the eraser and blob radii, anything comparing a SCREEN-space threshold against a DOCUMENT-space distance -- is still only ever exercised where zoom is 1.0. Mutation-measured: dropping the zoom division in pointer_event_payload reds exactly 2 of the 2668 Rust lib tests (the new gesture vector and the pre-existing recorder::fidelity lockstep_rect_draw_under_pan_zoom_is_faithful).
coverage_gaps.unblock: Per-family, and now cheap: add a `view` block to an existing case in each family whose tool reads a screen-space threshold. Highest value first -- a selection click/marquee at zoom != 1 (the hit radius), a path-eraser stroke (the historical bug), a paintbrush stroke (ditto). No machinery is needed for any of them.

coverage_gaps.title: LIVE DIVERGENCE, unpinnable here: zoom_in / zoom_out with no anchor params anchor at the viewport centre in Rust and at the canvas top-left corner in Swift
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit with a probe vector run through both action corpora, then deleted (it cannot land: pinning the spec value reds the swift lane, and pinning Swift's value would be a test whose expected value coincides with the bug). Seed view {zoom 2.0, offset (-100, -50), viewport 800x600}, action zoom_in with params {}. transcripts/ZOOM_TOOL.md 'Keyboard shortcuts and actions' (the table row reads 'Viewport center') and workspace/actions.yaml:302 both say the default anchor is the viewport centre, which gives (2.4, -200, -120) by that file's 'Anchor and clamp math' block. RUST PRODUCES EXACTLY THAT. Swift produces (2.4, -120, -60) -- the triple you get by anchoring at screen (0, 0). TWO independent causes, verified separately: (a) Swift's dispatchYamlAction does not merge an action's declared param DEFAULTS into the `param` scope, so `param.anchor_x` resolves to null -> 0 instead of the declared -1 (Rust does merge, and renderer.rs's dispatch_action_supplies_action_param_defaults_when_caller_omits names this exact failure -- 'putting the anchor at the canvas's upper-left corner'); and (b) even with -1 delivered, YamlToolEffects.swift:768's `anchorXRaw < 0 ? px : anchorXRaw` has no viewport-centre branch at all -- it falls back to the document origin's screen position and never reads the `viewportW` the Model carries. Fixing (a) alone moves Swift from (-120, -60) to (-100, -50); it does not reach the spec.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Every keyboard and View-menu zoom in Swift recentres on a different point from Rust. Only 3 of the 236 actions declare param defaults (zoom_in, zoom_out, artboards_panel_select), so cause (a)'s blast radius is small but includes a third verb no fixture covers.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Cause (b) lands in JasSwift/Sources/Tools/YamlToolEffects.swift, which was reserved by a concurrent wave when this was measured; cause (a) lands in LayersPanel.dispatchYamlAction and is a five-line merge, but landing it ALONE would leave the vector still red and so still unpinnable. Fix both, then move the probe vector into test_fixtures/actions/view_state.json -- the family, the seed and the expected_view assertion are already there and this is the vector they were built for.

coverage_gaps.title: LIVE DIVERGENCE, unpinnable here, and the SPEC SIDES WITH SWIFT: zoom_to_actual_size leaves the pan alone in Swift and recentres it in Rust
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit with the same deleted probe. Seed view {zoom 4.0, offset (-300, -200), viewport 800x600}, action zoom_to_actual_size. transcripts/ZOOM_TOOL.md says it twice -- the shortcut table's Centering column reads 'Pan unchanged', and the prose reads 'zoom_to_actual_size sets zoom_level = 1.0 and leaves view_offset_x / view_offset_y unchanged' -- and workspace/actions.yaml:337 repeats it ('leave pan unchanged'). That gives (1.0, -300, -200). SWIFT PRODUCES EXACTLY THAT. Rust produces (1.0, 225, 175): interpreter/effects.rs's doc.zoom.set recomputes the pan around the viewport centre, and its own comment cites a ZOOM_TOOL.md sentence ('whatever was under the viewport center stays approximately under it') that does not appear in that file -- grep for 'approximately' there returns nothing.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Ctrl+1 from a zoomed-in view shows a different region of the document in each port. It is also the one row here where the reference text and the behaviour someone deliberately changed point in opposite directions, so a reader who trusts either one alone will 'fix' the wrong port.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Needs a ruling before code, because the spec is not silent -- it is explicit and Rust contradicts it. If the ruling keeps 'pan unchanged', Rust's doc.zoom.set is the site (interpreter/effects.rs, reserved by a concurrent wave when this was measured) and the vector lands unchanged. If the ruling prefers Rust's recentring, the SAME COMMIT must rewrite both ZOOM_TOOL.md's table row and prose and actions.yaml's description, or the next reader reverts it. Either way the vector is already written and the machinery to run it is landed.

coverage_gaps.title: The six Swift View actions never reach the YAML pipeline on the user path, so the corpus can gate the effects and the app can still do something else
coverage_gaps.evidence: Re-verified by reading the call sites on this commit. Canvas/ContentView.swift:562-570 (dispatchToolOptionsAction) and Menu/JasCommands.swift:352-362 both switch on the action name and call native Model methods -- zoomIn / zoomOut / zoomToActualSize / fitActiveArtboard / fitAllArtboards / fitInWindow, Model.swift:569-621 -- instead of dispatching the action. Those methods hardcode what the workspace declares: zoom_step 1.2, min/max 0.1 / 64.0, fit padding 20.0, and fitActiveArtboard uses `document.artboards.first` where actions.yaml uses active_document.current_artboard (the topmost PANEL-SELECTED artboard, else the first). So preferences.viewport.* moves Rust and not Swift, and a panel-selected second artboard is fitted correctly by the corpus path and wrongly by the menu.
coverage_gaps.blocks: A fix applied to a doc.zoom.* effect passes the corpus and changes nothing a user can see. The view_state.json family drives Swift's dispatchYamlAction, which is the --test-fifo / dialog-footer / Artboards-panel route, NOT the menu or the keyboard.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Route both call sites through LayersPanel.dispatchYamlAction and delete the six Model methods -- which is the house rule that behaviour lives in workspace/*.yaml. BUT NOT YET, and the order matters: today the native zoomIn anchors at the viewport centre, which is what the spec asks for, while the YAML path in Swift anchors at the top-left corner (see view-anchor-default-divergence). Routing first would REGRESS the menu. Fix that row, then this one, then the fit_active_artboard panel-selection vector becomes writable too.

coverage_gaps.title: No corpus case can panel-select an artboard, so fit_active_artboard is only ever gated on the FIRST artboard
coverage_gaps.evidence: The action fixture format carries `selection` (canvas element paths, consumed by Controller::set_selection / setSelection) and nothing else; both runners' panel-selection arguments -- dispatchYamlAction's `artboardsPanelSelection`, Rust's equivalent -- are never fed from a fixture. Measured by reading run_action_case (jas_dioxus/src/recorder/replay.rs) and runActionModel (JasSwift/Tests/CrossLanguageTests.swift) on this commit. So view_state.json's fit_active_artboard_from_wrong_view vector resolves current_artboard to the first board, which is the ONE case where the divergence in view-actions-bypass-yaml-in-swift (artboards.first vs current_artboard) is invisible.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The 'topmost panel-selected artboard, else the artboard at position 1' rule in actions.yaml and ARTBOARDS.md is half-gated: the else-branch is pinned, the branch itself is not.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Teach both action runners an optional `artboards_panel_selection` block (a list of artboard ids) alongside the existing `selection`, then add a fit_active_artboard vector over two_artboards.svg selecting the SECOND board. two_artboards.svg already declares three boards with stable ids (ab1/ab2/ab3), so no new setup SVG is needed.

coverage_gaps.title: PARTLY CLOSED (BINDVALUE): bind.* values are now pinned for 3 of the 16 panels; the other 13 and panel enabled_when are not, and panel_layout still reduces resolved text to a scalar count
coverage_gaps.evidence: CLOSED HALF: test_fixtures/algorithms/panel_bind_values.json -- 4 vectors, 225 rows -- resolves bind expressions and pins the resulting STRINGS. Driven by all three live implementations: the reference (workspace_interpreter/tests/test_bind_values.py), Rust (cross_language_test.rs algorithm_bind_values_vectors) and Swift (CrossLanguageTests.swift testAlgorithmBindValues); both ports matched the reference-generated golden on their first run. Each of the three also asserts the census's own claim directly: the two data scopes differing ONLY in panel.hex ("664040" vs "664141") give byte-identical widget_tree output and byte-identical layout_panel rects, and differ in exactly one bind_values row (cp_hex, bind.value). OPEN HALF, counted over the compiled bundle: 311 declared bind entries across the 16 panels, of which 136 are in the three seeded panels (color 82, stroke 36, swatches 18) and 175 are not; the largest uncovered surfaces are paragraph (30) and character (24). Panel enabled_when is evaluated by no gate at all -- 3 nodes carry it, all in gradient_panel_content, all with the literal expression false. panel_layout itself is UNCHANGED and still length-only: text_w is eval_text(...).chars().count() * CHAR_WIDTH in jas_dioxus/src/interpreter/panel_layout.rs and resolved.unicodeScalars.count * charWidth in JasSwift/Sources/Interpreter/PanelLayout.swift.
coverage_gaps.blocks: A bind-value divergence in one of the 13 unseeded panels is still invisible, as is any divergence in a panel enabled_when. panel_widget_tree remains key-names-only by design (widening it would rewrite every record it emits), so nothing else covers those panels.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Fixture-only for the panel coverage: add BIND_SEED entries in scripts/gen_panel_layout_fixture.py and regenerate. enabled_when needs a one-line arm in each of the three bind_values implementations PLUS a seeded gradient vector -- and must not be added without the vector, since an unexercised arm is exactly the shape this list exists to keep visible.

coverage_gaps.title: art_along_path's first-subpath flattener is driven by no corpus family, and a leading ClosePath makes it discard the whole path in BOTH ports
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit through a throwaway probe in each port, then removed. flatten (jas_dioxus/src/algorithms/art_along_path.rs) and flattenArtPath (JasSwift/Sources/Algorithms/ArtAlongPath.swift) both return [] for d = [Z, M(3,2), L(13,2)], and [(3,2),(13,2)] for the same path without the leading Z. Both close arms are `if cx != sx || cy != sy { push(sx, sy) }` followed by an unconditional `return out`, and at a leading close cx == sx == cy == sy == 0, so the function returns the empty accumulator. The two ports AGREE, so no port-vs-port comparison can see it; and no fixture reaches either function, since neither roundtrip binary calls it -- grep for art_along_path / flattenArtPath in jas_dioxus/src/bin/algorithm_roundtrip.rs and JasSwift/ToolsAlgorithm/AlgorithmRoundtrip.swift matches 0 lines in each.
coverage_gaps.blocks: S-4 (a leading ClosePath is a no-op, ruled by JYH 2026-07-27) is honoured by flatten_path_commands in both ports and by flatten_path_to_rings, but NOT here: this flattener treats a leading close as end-of-first-subpath and drops the real subpath that follows, so an art / pattern-along-path / bristle brush applied to such a path flattens to nothing. It is a SHARED defect rather than a divergence, which is exactly the class a port-vs-port equivalence gate is blind to.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Needs a corpus family before a fix, per the fixture-first law: teach both roundtrip binaries an art-flatten verb over this function, add a leading-close vector, and only then decide whether the close arm should continue past a no-op close instead of returning.

coverage_gaps.title: Every boolean and compound-shape vector in the corpus runs on operands with NO id, so the identity half of the preservation law is invisible at exactly the arms that legislate it
coverage_gaps.evidence: Enumerated on this commit by parsing all of test_fixtures/actions/*.json and test_fixtures/operations/*.json for cases whose body mentions boolean or compound: 8 vectors, drawing on 4 setup SVGs (overlapping_rects.svg, two_rects.svg, boolean_collinear_union.svg, compound_and_rect.svg). grep -o for an id= attribute over those four files returns ZERO hits, and none of them sets name, opacity, transform, mask, fill-rule, gradient, width profile, stroke brush or tool origin on an operand either. Driven consequence, measured this round: apply_destructive_boolean's UNION arm carried the FRONTMOST operand's whole CommonProps -- id included -- through an N->1 merge, and make_compound_shape_with_op put the frontmost's id on the wrapper while that operand stayed a child (an id walk yielded [id-front, id-back, id-front]). Both were fixed in the IDENTITY wave of 2026-07-27 WITHOUT ONE GOLDEN BYTE MOVING.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The frontmost-id violation could be fixed, unfixed or inverted between the two ports and no cross-language golden would notice. Rust now mints a fresh id at the N->1 arm when an operand carried one; JasSwift's applyDestructiveBoolean drops id/name/toolOrigin/mask entirely and writes locked false. That LIVE divergence is real and is currently unseeable, because it manifests only on operands with attributes no vector sets.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Fixture work, in this order (it is condition (a) of transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md's ratification condition): add an attribute-rich boolean setup SVG carrying ids, names, transform, mask, opacity, blend mode, fill rule, gradient, width profile, stroke brush and tool origin on both operands; add union/intersection/exclude and subtract-survivor vectors over it; and assert id FRESHNESS (result id not in the pre-edit id set) rather than a literal id. The action lane already installs the deterministic mint override (recorder::replay::run_action_case), so a literal id is pinnable there; the OPERATIONS lane does NOT install it, so a minting op in that lane is non-deterministic today and needs either the override or a value-in-op id first. Neither can land until JasSwift's boolean rebuild is brought to the same rule -- until then the vector would simply red the swift lane.

coverage_gaps.title: No gesture vector reaches a control-point drag, so the whole partial-selection promotion path -- including Rect -> Polygon -- has zero cross-language coverage
coverage_gaps.evidence: The gesture corpus declares 9 tools on this commit (blob_brush, ellipse, line, paintbrush, polygon, rect, rounded_rect, selection, star); partial_selection is not among them, and the two selection vectors are select_marquee and select_click, neither of which presses a control point. grep -rl for partial_selection over test_fixtures/ returns only toolbar/shortcut structure and key-resolution fixtures -- no gesture. Separately, exactly ONE rounded rect exists anywhere in test_fixtures/svg/ (complex_document.svg, rx=ry=13.3333) and no vector drags its corners.
coverage_gaps.blocks: move_control_points' Rect arm is a cross-kind copy site where the compiler demands each field and a human answers it; it dropped both gradients on a 1->1 kind change and discarded rx/ry with no ruling, and no corpus family could see either. The 2026-07-27 IDENTITY wave fixed both in Rust (gradients forwarded; rx/ry flattened into the emitted points per JYH's ratified answer (3)), which means Rust and JasSwift now DISAGREE on the promotion of a ROUNDED rect -- Swift still emits four square corners -- and nothing in the corpus can say so.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Machinery first, then fixtures: the gesture runners must be able to seed a Partial control-point selection and dispatch the partial_selection tool, which no runner does today. Then a corner-drag vector over a rounded, gradient-filled rect pins the promotion in both ports at once. Landing the vector before JasSwift's moveControlPoints Rect arm flattens rx/ry would simply red the swift lane.
